question.text: Assume the following round-trip ETIRD trading cost components for a stem-based calculation: Brokerage Rs. 400, Exchange charges Rs. 150, Clearing charges Rs. 50, SEBI fees Rs. 10. The stem also specifies that GST at 18% applies only on brokerage plus exchange and clearing charges. Under these stated assumptions, what is the total all-in cost?

explanation.text: The Logic: Base costs = 400 + 150 + 50 + 10 = Rs. 610. Using the stem's assumption that GST applies only on brokerage + exchange charges + clearing charges, GST base = 400 + 150 + 50 = Rs. 600 and GST = 18% of 600 = Rs. 108. Total all-in = 610 + 108 = Rs. 718. The Trap: Rs. 610 ignores GST. Rs. 682 incorrectly applies GST to the SEBI fees too. Rs. 750 uses 25% instead of the stated 18%. Note: The Series IV workbook lists trading cost categories — statutory levies (such as GST), regulatory levies (such as SEBI/exchange/clearing charges), brokerage, and SEBI turnover fees — but does not itself specify the GST base or rate used here. Confirm the applicable GST base from current statutory notifications when applying this calculation outside this stem.
